text:
maya: flagged by internal audit: backup-restore job left plaintext snapshot files on shared EFS at /mnt/restore/tmp/ while performing a customer restore. Found by file-scan job at 2026-04-12T08:12Z.

forensics-bot: :warning: FILE_EXPOSED - /mnt/restore/tmp/snap-20260412-abc123.bin discovered world-readable. Alert FSEC-20260412-09

rahul: how many files and who mounted the share?

maya: initial grep shows 9 files from the restore window 08:05-08:10. CloudTrail shows backup-restore role performed kms:Decrypt ~08:06 for key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/legacy-1111. Sample CT entry: 
```
2026-04-12T08:06:17Z kms:Decrypt userIdentity:AssumedRole:backup-restore-prod resource:arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/legacy-1111
```

rahul: why were plaintext blobs written to EFS? The restore agent should stream and zero memory.

sophie: I deployed an agent change two days ago to support concurrent chunked restores. It writes chunk files to disk before streaming to client to reduce memory pressure. I thought those were created with 0600 perms and immediately unlinked after use.

maya: audit shows they were created with 0666 due to umask override in the systemd unit inherited from the older restore-runner service. That explains world-readable.

ops-bot: hint: recent RBAC/ops change rolled in at 2026-04-11T23:00 which added a new k8s daemonset to mount the EFS for monitoring; the daemonset used runAsUser:1000 and set fsGroup:0. Possibly widened access.

rahul: immediate mitigation: 1) revoke access to the EFS mount by scaling down the monitoring daemonset, 2) identify and securely shred the exposed files (overwrite unlink), 3) rotate affected CMK or rewrap data keys if needed, 4) notify compliance.

sophie: I'm disabling the new agent concurrent-chunked-restore flag and reverting unit file to enforce umask 0077. Pushing hotfix now.

maya: forensics: can you confirm whether any external principals accessed those files (S3 GETs or NFS client IPs) between creation and discovery?

forensics-bot: checked NFS logs and mount table. Only internal restore workers and the monitoring daemonset had mounts. No external IPs. No S3 GETs (objects were not in object-store, only temporary on EFS).

rahul: good. Still a severe finding: customer data was momentarily world-readable inside our VPC. Compliance will want timeline and controls.

compliance-bot: action: create incident record INC-20260412-09; required artifacts: file list, creation timestamps, KMS decrypt logs, who deployed agent change, RBAC/daemonset change PRs.

maya: file list and CT snippets attached to incident channel. Shredding script executed: shred -u -z -n 3 <file>. Confirmed removed.

ops-bot: scaled down monitoring-daemonset to 0 replicas. EFS access restricted via security-group and POSIX ACLs tightened.

rahul: CMK rotation decision: because plaintext was only on EFS (not persisted to object-store) and KMS Decrypts were valid for the restore, rotate not strictly required. But to be conservative we will schedule rewrap of that customer's snapshot envelope keys. I'll open ticket to rewrap keys and document rationale.

maya: postmortem owners: agent revert and umask fix (sophie), daemonset RBAC revert + SG/ACL hardening (ops), forensics timeline & artifacts (maya), compliance brief & customer comms decision (compliance).

sophie: hotfix deployed to prod and umask enforced. Running local e2e to ensure no leftover temp files.

maya: thanks. Follow-up: add CI check that any code writing temp plaintext enforces file mode 0600 and immediate secure-unlink on completion, add admission controller to block pods mounting EFS with fsGroup=0 and require explicit POSIX ACLs.

rahul: agreed. We'll also add an audit rule to flag any kms:Decrypt events correlated with EFS file creation within 5 minutes to detect similar patterns.

compliance-bot: incident created and assigned. Will prepare SOC2 note after review.

(ends)
